title: A Chess Loop
reviewNotes: Three branches, 15 exact positions from the seven-piece phase after ...Kxg4 at 115 seconds. Nc6 attacks Rd8 and guards promotion. Kxe7 clears the way for protected Nd8/Nf7 interpositions, then b8=Q wins. Corrects captioned Rh1 to Rh8 and Kxc7 to Kxe7. Both guarded premature promotion (followed by ...Rxb8 Nxb8) and independent unguarded promotion lose exactly. Earlier eight-piece loop remains context.

And there is no easy way for the black rook to find another path to the pawn. So, the pawn is simply going to promote. But of course, the rook can try to go to E1 and come around this way. Now pushing the pawn is not good enough. After rook to B1, the rook is going to stop the promotion. And the knight is now stranded defending the pawn forever. But of course, black can pick up this pawn and now make sure that white's only chance is this pawn that seems to have been already neutralized. >> [music] >> But white has a plan that continues with knight to c6, now attacking the rook and defending the promotion square. The rook has to stay on the eighth rank, so it will have to go to h1. Of course, getting the queen now would make no sense because yes, you get rid of the rook, but you only have a knight left.
